newsitem.title: GERMANY: Delta aims to raise European cargo revenues.
newsitem.headline: Delta aims to raise European cargo revenues.

text.p: Delta Air Lines said it aims to improve ex-Europe cargo revenues by 15 percent in the 1996-97 fiscal year.
Danita Waterfall, Delta's regional director cargo sales and services Europe, told Reuters in an interview: "Out of Europe our capacities are running at about 65 percent."
"Our goal in this fiscal year is to increase revenues 15 percent," she added.
She declined, however, to disclose any absolute figures for European cargo tonnage or revenue for the past July 1-June 30 fiscal year.
Frankfurt-based Waterfall said Germany is the largest cargo market for Delta in Europe, followed by Britain and France.

Delta now guarantees same-day delivery from its 30 Europe online stations to U.S. destinations with the introduction of its new Cargo Booking and Management System and Priority First time-definite product.

Waterfall said: "In Europe we are selling Priority First and we can guarantee to our freight forwarders they have so much space and it will definitely get here at this time. Because of this booking system, we bump domestic freight.
"Now you can book from any European city to the final destination. It used to be that when freight got to a gateway city, onward (transport) was by chance," she added.
The system also allows barcoding of all export shipments which cuts transit time at U.S. hubs dramatically, she said.
"Now freight forwarders can pick up five or six hours earlier. It is guaranteed same-day service," she stressed.

The system also allows Delta to take individual consolidation items and ship them directly to fill empty space, as well as to offer a tracing system. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017 ==
